question:
A small conducting loop is placed coaxially in front of the open end of a long solenoid. At the loop position, the solenoid’s magnetic field points out of the solenoid (towards the loop) and is increasing with time. The loop is free to move along the common axis.

Neglect self-inductance of the loop. As seen from the solenoid end (looking towards the loop), the induced current in the loop and the initial force on the loop due to the solenoid’s non-uniform field are respectively:

options.A: Clockwise, and the loop is attracted towards the solenoid
options.B: Clockwise, and the loop is repelled away from the solenoid
options.C: Anticlockwise, and the loop is attracted towards the solenoid
options.D: Anticlockwise, and the loop is repelled away from the solenoid
